pt.R: Quando os amonitas viram que os arameus tinham fugido, eles também fugiram de Abisai, irmão de Joabe, e voltaram para dentro da sua cidade. Então Joabe voltou para casa, em Jerusalém.

decisions.choice: differences from 2 Samuel 10:14
decisions.reason: Chronicles adds "also" and "his brother". Where Samuel says "Joab returned from fighting the sons of Ammon and came to Jerusalem", Chronicles says only "Joab came to Jerusalem".

decisions.choice: they went into the city, and Joab went to Jerusalem: a victory, but not yet a conquest
decisions.reason: The Ammonites were safe behind their city walls, and Joab did not stay to besiege it. The siege of Rabbah came the next spring (20:1-3).

decisions.choice: his brother: Joab's brother
decisions.reason: "His" refers back to Joab, who is named in verse 14 and again at the end of this verse.

decisions.choice: Joab's brother
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name Joab, since "his brother" could otherwise seem to point to someone in this verse.

decisions.choice: também; seu irmão / irmão de Joabe; Joabe foi a Jerusalém
decisions.reason: 2 Samuel 10:14 in Portuguese with Chronicles' "also" and "his brother" (m1, m3), and without "voltou de [lutar] contra os filhos de Amom"; Balanced and Readable keep "voltou", as the English says "went home".

source.text: וַיַּ֣רְא אֲרָ֗ם כִּ֣י נִגְּפוּ֮ לִפְנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵל֒ וַֽיִּשְׁלְחוּ֙ מַלְאָכִ֔ים וַיּוֹצִ֣יאוּ אֶת־אֲרָ֔ם אֲשֶׁ֖ר מֵעֵ֣בֶר הַנָּהָ֑ר וְשׁוֹפַ֛ךְ שַׂר־צְבָ֥א הֲדַדְעֶ֖זֶר לִפְנֵיהֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And saw Aram that they had been defeated before Israel, and they sent messengers and brought out Aram which [was] from beyond the River; and Shophach commander of [the] army of Hadadezer [was] before them.

en.L: And Aram saw that they had been defeated before Israel, and they sent messengers and brought out the Arameans who [were] beyond the River; and Shophach the commander of the army of Hadadezer [was] before them.
en.B: When the Arameans saw that they had been beaten by Israel, they sent messengers and brought out the Arameans who were beyond the Euphrates River, with Shophach, the commander of Hadadezer's army, at their head.
en.R: The Arameans saw that Israel had beaten them. So they sent messengers to bring more Arameans from the other side of the Euphrates River. Shophach, the commander of Hadadezer's army, led them.

es.L: Y vio Aram que había sido derrotado delante de Israel, y enviaron mensajeros e hicieron salir a los arameos que [estaban] al otro lado del Río; y Sofac, jefe del ejército de Hadad-ezer, [iba] delante de ellos.
es.B: Cuando los arameos vieron que Israel los había derrotado, enviaron mensajeros y trajeron a los arameos que estaban al otro lado del río Éufrates, con Sofac, el jefe del ejército de Hadad-ezer, al frente de ellos.
es.R: Los arameos vieron que Israel los había vencido. Así que enviaron mensajeros para traer más arameos del otro lado del río Éufrates. Sofac, el jefe del ejército de Hadad-ezer, los dirigía.

fr.L: Et Aram vit qu’ils avaient été battus devant Israël, et ils envoyèrent des messagers et firent sortir les Araméens qui [étaient] au-delà du Fleuve ; et Shophak, le chef de l’armée d’Hadadézer, [était] à leur tête.
fr.B: Quand les Araméens virent qu’ils avaient été battus par Israël, ils envoyèrent des messagers chercher les Araméens qui étaient de l’autre côté de l’Euphrate, avec à leur tête Shophak, le chef de l’armée d’Hadadézer.
fr.R: Les Araméens ont vu qu’Israël les avait battus. Alors ils ont envoyé des messagers pour faire venir d’autres Araméens de l’autre côté de l’Euphrate. Shophak, le chef de l’armée d’Hadadézer, les commandait.

sw.L: Aramu walipoona kwamba wameshindwa mbele ya Israeli, wakatuma wajumbe wakawatoa Waaramu [waliokuwa] ng'ambo ya Mto; naye Shofaki jemadari wa jeshi la Hadadezeri [alikuwa] mbele yao.
sw.B: Waaramu walipoona kwamba wameshindwa na Israeli, walituma wajumbe wakawaleta Waaramu waliokuwa ng'ambo ya mto Frati, naye Shofaki, mkuu wa jeshi la Hadadezeri, akawaongoza.
sw.R: Waaramu waliona kwamba Israeli wamewashinda. Basi wakatuma wajumbe kuleta Waaramu zaidi kutoka ng'ambo ya mto Frati. Shofaki, mkuu wa jeshi la Hadadezeri, akawaongoza.

vi.L: A-ram thấy mình đã bị đánh bại trước mặt Y-sơ-ra-ên, thì sai sứ giả đem người A-ram ở bên kia Sông ra; Sô-phác, tướng chỉ huy quân đội của Ha-đa-đê-xe, đi trước họ.
vi.B: Khi người A-ram thấy mình đã bị Y-sơ-ra-ên đánh bại, họ sai sứ giả đi gọi người A-ram ở bên kia sông Ơ-phơ-rát đến, có Sô-phác, tướng chỉ huy quân đội của Ha-đa-đê-xe, dẫn đầu.
vi.R: Người A-ram thấy Y-sơ-ra-ên đã đánh bại mình. Vì vậy họ sai sứ giả đi gọi thêm người A-ram ở bên kia sông Ơ-phơ-rát đến. Sô-phác, tướng chỉ huy quân đội của Ha-đa-đê-xe, dẫn đầu họ.

ko.L: 그리고 아람이 자기들이 이스라엘 앞에서 졌다는 것을 보고, 사자들을 보내어 강 건너편에 [있는] 아람을 불러냈다. 그리고 하닷에셀의 군대 사령관 소박이 그들 앞에 [있었다].
ko.B: 아람 사람들은 자기들이 이스라엘에게 졌다는 것을 알고, 사자들을 보내 유프라테스 강 건너편에 있는 아람 사람들을 불러냈다. 하닷에셀의 군대 사령관 소박이 그들을 거느렸다.
ko.R: 아람 사람들은 이스라엘에게 졌다는 것을 알았다. 그래서 그들은 사자들을 보내 유프라테스 강 건너편에서 아람 사람들을 더 불러왔다. 하닷에셀의 군대 사령관 소박이 그들을 이끌었다.

pt.L: E Arã viu que tinham sido derrotados diante de Israel, e enviaram mensageiros e fizeram sair os arameus que [estavam] do outro lado do Rio; e Sofaque, o comandante do exército de Hadadezer, [estava] à frente deles.
pt.B: Quando os arameus viram que tinham sido derrotados por Israel, enviaram mensageiros e fizeram sair os arameus que viviam do outro lado do rio Eufrates, tendo à frente Sofaque, o comandante do exército de Hadadezer.
pt.R: Os arameus viram que Israel os tinha derrotado. Por isso mandaram mensageiros para trazer mais arameus do outro lado do rio Eufrates. Sofaque, o comandante do exército de Hadadezer, os liderava.

decisions.choice: a shorter form of 2 Samuel 10:15-16, with the name Shophach
decisions.reason: 2 Samuel 10:15-16 says the Arameans gathered together, that Hadadezer sent and brought out the Arameans beyond the River, and that they came to Helam. Chronicles says the defeated Arameans themselves sent messengers, and does not name Helam. Samuel spells the commander's name Shobach; Chronicles has Shophach. The two forms are the same name spelled differently.

decisions.choice: defeated: struck down in battle
decisions.reason: The verb means to be struck, and is used of an army routed by its enemy (1 Samuel 4:2, 10).

decisions.choice: the River: the Euphrates
decisions.reason: "The River" with no other name means the Euphrates (Genesis 31:21; Joshua 24:2). The Arameans living on its far side were under Hadadezer's power (18:3).

decisions.choice: Hadadezer: the king of Zobah of chapter 18
decisions.reason: Hadadezer was the strongest Aramean ruler of the time (18:3-8). Chapter 18 sums up David's victory over him, and this chapter tells how that war began.

decisions.choice: the Euphrates River; more Arameans (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the river, which the Hebrew calls simply "the River". Readable says "more Arameans", since these were fresh troops called up after the first defeat.

decisions.choice: Sofac
decisions.reason: Chronicles spells the commander's name differently from 2 Samuel 10:16 (Sobac); the Spanish follows each book's form.

decisions.choice: "Shophak"
decisions.reason: Chronicles spells the commander’s name differently from Samuel, and French keeps each book’s spelling, as the English does.

decisions.choice: Shofaki
decisions.reason: Chronicles spells the commander "Shophach" where 2 Samuel 10:16 has "Shobach"; the Swahili keeps each book's spelling.

decisions.choice: "Sô-phác"
decisions.reason: Chronicles spells the commander's name differently from 2 Samuel, so the Vietnamese name differs too, as the English does.

decisions.choice: Sofaque; o Rio (L), o rio Eufrates (B, R)
decisions.reason: 2 Samuel 10:15-16 in Portuguese where the words are the same ("o Rio" at Literal, "o rio Eufrates" at Balanced and Readable), shortened as Chronicles shortens it, without Helã (m1). Chronicles spells the commander's name with a different consonant from Samuel's Shobach ("Sobaque" in 2 Samuel 10:16), so Portuguese writes "Sofaque", the same name in Chronicles' form.

source.text: וַיֻּגַּ֣ד לְדָוִ֗יד וַיֶּאֱסֹ֤ף אֶת־כָּל־יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ וַיַּעֲבֹ֣ר הַיַּרְדֵּ֔ן וַיָּבֹ֣א אֲלֵהֶ֔ם וַֽיַּעֲרֹ֖ךְ אֲלֵהֶ֑ם וַיַּעֲרֹ֨ךְ דָּוִ֜יד לִקְרַ֤את אֲרָם֙ מִלְחָמָ֔ה וַיִּֽלָּחֲמ֖וּ עִמּֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And it was told to David, and he gathered all Israel and crossed the Jordan and came to them and drew up against them; and drew up David to meet Aram [for] battle, and they fought with him.

en.L: And it was told to David, and he gathered all Israel and crossed the Jordan and came to them and drew up against them. And David drew up [for] battle to meet Aram, and they fought with him.
en.B: When David was told, he gathered all Israel, crossed the Jordan, came up to them, and formed his lines against them. David drew up his army for battle against the Arameans, and they fought with him.
en.R: When David heard about it, he called together all the fighting men of Israel. They crossed the Jordan River and marched up to the Arameans and got into battle lines facing them. When David's army was ready for battle, the Arameans fought against him.

es.L: Y se lo informaron a David, y reunió a todo Israel y cruzó el Jordán y llegó a ellos y se puso en orden de batalla contra ellos. Y David se puso en orden de batalla frente a Aram, y pelearon contra él.
es.B: Cuando se lo dijeron a David, reunió a todo Israel, cruzó el Jordán, llegó hasta ellos y formó sus líneas contra ellos. David puso a su ejército en orden de batalla frente a los arameos, y ellos pelearon contra él.
es.R: Cuando David se enteró, reunió a todos los guerreros de Israel. Cruzaron el río Jordán, llegaron hasta los arameos y se pusieron en formación frente a ellos. Cuando el ejército de David estuvo listo para la batalla, los arameos pelearon contra él.

fr.L: Et on l’annonça à David, et il rassembla tout Israël, et passa le Jourdain, et vint vers eux, et se rangea contre eux. Et David se rangea en bataille face à Aram, et ils combattirent contre lui.
fr.B: Quand on en informa David, il rassembla tout Israël, passa le Jourdain, arriva jusqu’à eux et se rangea en bataille contre eux. David disposa son armée pour le combat face aux Araméens, et ceux-ci lui livrèrent combat.
fr.R: Quand David l’a appris, il a réuni tous les combattants d’Israël. Ils ont traversé le Jourdain, ils sont arrivés près des Araméens et ils se sont mis en ordre de bataille face à eux. Quand l’armée de David a été prête pour le combat, les Araméens l’ont attaqué.

sw.L: Daudi akaambiwa, naye akawakusanya Israeli wote akavuka Yordani akawafikia akajipanga dhidi yao. Daudi akajipanga [kwa] vita kukabiliana na Aramu, nao wakapigana naye.
sw.B: Daudi alipoambiwa, aliwakusanya Israeli wote, akavuka Yordani, akawafikia, akajipanga dhidi yao. Daudi akapanga jeshi lake kwa vita dhidi ya Waaramu, nao wakapigana naye.
sw.R: Daudi aliposikia habari hiyo, aliwaita pamoja wapiganaji wote wa Israeli. Wakavuka mto Yordani, wakawaendea Waaramu, wakajipanga kwa vita kuwakabili. Jeshi la Daudi lilipokuwa tayari kwa vita, Waaramu wakapigana naye.

vi.L: Người ta báo cho Đa-vít, thì ông tập hợp toàn thể Y-sơ-ra-ên, vượt sông Giô-đanh, đến cùng họ và dàn trận đối đầu với họ. Đa-vít dàn trận đối đầu với A-ram, và họ giao chiến với ông.
vi.B: Khi được báo tin, Đa-vít tập hợp toàn thể Y-sơ-ra-ên, vượt sông Giô-đanh, tiến đến chỗ họ và dàn trận đối đầu với họ. Đa-vít dàn quân ra trận đối đầu với người A-ram, và họ giao chiến với ông.
vi.R: Khi Đa-vít nghe tin ấy, ông triệu tập tất cả chiến sĩ của Y-sơ-ra-ên. Họ vượt sông Giô-đanh, tiến đến chỗ người A-ram và dàn trận đối mặt với họ. Khi quân của Đa-vít đã sẵn sàng chiến đấu, người A-ram giao chiến với ông.

ko.L: 그리고 [그것이] 다윗에게 알려지자, 그가 온 이스라엘을 모아 요단을 건너 그들에게 이르러 그들과 맞서 전열을 갖추었다. 그리고 다윗이 아람과 맞서 싸우려고 전열을 갖추자, 그들이 그와 싸웠다.
ko.B: 이 소식이 다윗에게 전해지자, 그는 온 이스라엘을 모아 요단강을 건너 그들에게 이르러 그들과 맞서 전열을 갖추었다. 다윗이 아람 사람들과 맞서 싸우려고 전열을 갖추자, 그들이 그와 싸웠다.
ko.R: 다윗은 이 소식을 듣고 이스라엘의 군인들을 모두 불러 모았다. 그들은 요단강을 건너 아람 사람들에게 가서, 그들과 맞서 싸울 준비를 했다. 다윗의 군대가 싸울 준비를 마치자, 아람 사람들이 그와 싸웠다.

pt.L: E foi contado a Davi, e ele reuniu todo o Israel, e atravessou o Jordão, e veio a eles, e se pôs em ordem contra eles. E Davi se pôs em ordem de batalha contra Arã, e lutaram com ele.
pt.B: Quando isso foi contado a Davi, ele reuniu todo o Israel, atravessou o Jordão, chegou até eles e formou as suas linhas contra eles. Davi pôs o seu exército em ordem de batalha contra os arameus, e eles lutaram com ele.
pt.R: Quando Davi soube disso, chamou todos os homens de Israel que podiam lutar. Eles atravessaram o rio Jordão, foram até os arameus e se colocaram em posição de batalha diante deles. Quando o exército de Davi estava pronto para a batalha, os arameus lutaram contra ele.

decisions.choice: David came to them and drew up: 2 Samuel 10:17 has "came to Helam" and "Aram drew up"
decisions.reason: Samuel says David came to Helam and the Arameans drew up their lines to meet him. Chronicles does not name the place, says David came "to them", and makes David the one who draws up the battle lines, twice over. Both books end the same way: the Arameans fought with him.

decisions.choice: all Israel: the whole fighting force of the nation
decisions.reason: This time David calls up the full army and leads it himself, because the Arameans have brought fresh forces from beyond the Euphrates.

decisions.choice: drew up against them, and David drew up: the same act told twice
decisions.reason: The second clause repeats the first and names David, making clear who set the battle in order before the fighting began.

decisions.choice: all the fighting men of Israel
decisions.reason: Readable says who "all Israel" were in a battle story: the men who could fight, as in 2 Samuel 10:17.

decisions.choice: veio a eles; Davi se pôs em ordem de batalha
decisions.reason: 2 Samuel 10:17 in Portuguese up to "o Jordão" and from "lutaram com ele" ("todos os homens de Israel que podiam lutar" at Readable); between them Chronicles has David come "to them" and draw up the lines twice, instead of Helã and the Arameans drawing up (m1, m3).

source.text: וַיָּ֣נָס אֲרָם֮ מִלִּפְנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵל֒ וַיַּהֲרֹ֨ג דָּוִ֜יד מֵאֲרָ֗ם שִׁבְעַ֤ת אֲלָפִים֙ רֶ֔כֶב וְאַרְבָּעִ֥ים אֶ֖לֶף אִ֣ישׁ רַגְלִ֑י וְאֵ֛ת שׁוֹפַ֥ךְ שַֽׂר־הַצָּבָ֖א הֵמִֽית׃

records.literal_gloss: And fled Aram from before Israel, and killed David of Aram seven thousand chariot[s] and forty thousand men on foot; and Shophach commander of the army he put to death.

en.L: And Aram fled before Israel, and David killed of Aram [the men of] 7,000 chariots and 40,000 men on foot; and he put to death Shophach the commander of the army.
en.B: But the Arameans fled before Israel, and David killed 7,000 of their charioteers and 40,000 foot soldiers. He also put to death Shophach, the commander of their army.
en.R: But the Arameans ran away from the Israelites. David and his army killed 7,000 Aramean soldiers who fought from chariots and 40,000 soldiers on foot. They also killed Shophach, the commander of the Aramean army.

es.L: Y huyó Aram delante de Israel, y mató David de Aram [a los hombres de] 7 000 carros y a 40 000 hombres de a pie; y dio muerte a Sofac, jefe del ejército.
es.B: Pero los arameos huyeron delante de Israel, y David mató a 7 000 de sus hombres de los carros y a 40 000 soldados de a pie. También dio muerte a Sofac, el jefe de su ejército.
es.R: Pero los arameos huyeron de los israelitas. David y su ejército mataron a 7 000 soldados arameos que peleaban desde carros y a 40 000 soldados de a pie. También mataron a Sofac, el jefe del ejército arameo.

fr.L: Et Aram s’enfuit devant Israël, et David tua d’Aram [les hommes de] 7 000 chars et 40 000 hommes à pied ; et il fit mourir Shophak, le chef de l’armée.
fr.B: Mais les Araméens s’enfuirent devant Israël, et David tua les équipages de 7 000 de leurs chars et 40 000 fantassins. Il fit aussi mourir Shophak, le chef de leur armée.
fr.R: Mais les Araméens se sont enfuis devant les Israélites. David et son armée ont tué 7 000 soldats araméens qui combattaient sur des chars et 40 000 soldats à pied. Ils ont aussi tué Shophak, le chef de l’armée araméenne.

sw.L: Aramu wakakimbia mbele ya Israeli, naye Daudi akaua katika Aramu [watu wa] magari 7,000 na watu waendao kwa miguu 40,000; akamwua Shofaki jemadari wa jeshi.
sw.B: Lakini Waaramu walikimbia mbele ya Israeli, naye Daudi akaua watu 7,000 wa magari yao ya vita na askari wa miguu 40,000. Akamwua pia Shofaki, mkuu wa jeshi lao.
sw.R: Lakini Waaramu waliwakimbia Waisraeli. Daudi na jeshi lake wakawaua askari 7,000 wa Kiaramu waliopigana kutoka kwenye magari ya vita na askari 40,000 wa miguu. Wakamwua pia Shofaki, mkuu wa jeshi la Waaramu.

vi.L: A-ram chạy trốn trước mặt Y-sơ-ra-ên, và Đa-vít giết của A-ram [quân của] 7.000 cỗ xe và 40.000 bộ binh; ông cũng giết Sô-phác, tướng chỉ huy quân đội.
vi.B: Nhưng người A-ram bỏ chạy trước mặt Y-sơ-ra-ên, và Đa-vít giết 7.000 quân lính trên xe và 40.000 bộ binh của họ. Ông cũng giết Sô-phác, tướng chỉ huy quân đội của họ.
vi.R: Nhưng người A-ram bỏ chạy trước quân Y-sơ-ra-ên. Đa-vít và quân của ông giết 7.000 lính A-ram chiến đấu trên xe và 40.000 lính bộ. Họ cũng giết Sô-phác, tướng chỉ huy quân đội A-ram.

ko.L: 그리고 아람이 이스라엘 앞에서 도망쳤다. 그리고 다윗이 아람에서 병거 7,000[대의 군사]와 보병 40,000명을 죽였다. 그리고 그가 군대 사령관 소박을 죽였다.
ko.B: 그러나 아람 사람들은 이스라엘 앞에서 도망쳤다. 다윗은 아람의 병거 7,000대를 탄 군사들과 보병 40,000명을 죽였다. 또 군대 사령관 소박도 죽였다.
ko.R: 그러나 아람 사람들은 이스라엘 사람들 앞에서 달아났다. 다윗과 그의 군대는 병거를 타고 싸우던 아람 군사 7,000명과 걸어서 싸우던 군인 40,000명을 죽였다. 그들은 아람 군대 사령관 소박도 죽였다.

pt.L: E Arã fugiu diante de Israel, e Davi matou de Arã [os homens de] sete mil carros e quarenta mil homens de infantaria; e fez morrer Sofaque, o comandante do exército.
pt.B: Mas os arameus fugiram diante de Israel, e Davi matou sete mil dos seus condutores de carros e quarenta mil soldados de infantaria. Ele também matou Sofaque, o comandante do exército deles.
pt.R: Mas os arameus fugiram dos israelitas. Davi e o seu exército mataram sete mil soldados arameus que lutavam em carros de guerra e quarenta mil soldados de infantaria. Também mataram Sofaque, o comandante do exército arameu.

decisions.choice: 7,000 chariot men and 40,000 foot soldiers: 2 Samuel 10:18 has 700 chariots and 40,000 horsemen
decisions.reason: Samuel has seven hundred chariots and forty thousand horsemen; Chronicles has seven thousand chariot men and forty thousand men on foot. Numbers were easily miscopied, and either book may have kept the original figure. The word for "thousand" may also name a military unit, as noted at Numbers 1, which would make the forces smaller.

decisions.choice: chariots: the men who fought from them
decisions.reason: The word means chariots or chariotry. Since David "killed" them, the sense is the crews of the chariots.

decisions.choice: David killed: David's army, led by the king
decisions.reason: As often in battle reports, the king is named for the army he leads (18:1-5).

decisions.choice: he put Shophach to death: killed in the battle or afterward
decisions.reason: The verb means "caused to die" and does not say whether Shophach fell in the fighting or was executed after it. 2 Samuel 10:18 says David struck him down and he died there.

decisions.choice: David and his army
decisions.reason: Readable makes clear that David did not kill them alone, as in 2 Samuel 10:18.

decisions.choice: [the men of] 7,000 chariots (Literal); 7,000 charioteers (Balanced); soldiers who fought from chariots (Readable)
decisions.reason: The levels say that the men were killed, which is what the word means here.

decisions.choice: magari 7,000; watu waendao kwa miguu 40,000
decisions.reason: Chronicles has 7,000 chariots and 40,000 foot soldiers where 2 Samuel 10:18 has 700 and 40,000 horsemen; the Swahili follows Chronicles' figures, as the English does.

decisions.choice: "병거 7,000[대의 군사]" (L), "병거 7,000대를 탄 군사들" (B), "병거를 타고 싸우던 아람 군사 7,000명" (R)
decisions.reason: The levels say that the men were killed, as the English does; Chronicles has 7,000 and "men on foot" where 2 Samuel 10:18 has 700 and horsemen.

decisions.choice: sete mil; homens de infantaria (L), soldados de infantaria (B, R); fez morrer (L)
decisions.reason: 2 Samuel 10:18 in Portuguese ("[os homens de]" at Literal, "condutores" at Balanced, "Davi e o seu exército" at Readable), with Chronicles' numbers and troops (m1): "sete mil" chariot crews and "quarenta mil" men on foot instead of seven hundred and forty thousand horsemen. Literal says "fez morrer" for the causative verb (m4), which does not say how Sofaque died, so 2 Samuel's "e ele morreu ali" is left out.

source.text: וַיִּרְא֞וּ עַבְדֵ֣י הֲדַדְעֶ֗זֶר כִּ֤י נִגְּפוּ֙ לִפְנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וַיַּשְׁלִ֥ימוּ עִם־דָּוִ֖יד וַיַּֽעַבְדֻ֑הוּ וְלֹא־אָבָ֣ה אֲרָ֔ם לְהוֹשִׁ֥יעַ אֶת־בְּנֵי־עַמּ֖וֹן עֽוֹד׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And saw [the] servants of Hadadezer that they had been defeated before Israel, and they made peace with David and served him; and not was willing Aram to help [the] sons of Ammon again.

en.L: And the servants of Hadadezer saw that they had been defeated before Israel, and they made peace with David and served him. And Aram was not willing to help the sons of Ammon anymore.
en.B: When those who were subject to Hadadezer saw that Israel had defeated them, they made peace with David and became his subjects. After this the Arameans were not willing to give the Ammonites any more help.
en.R: The people who had served Hadadezer saw that Israel had beaten them. So they made peace with David and served him instead. After that, the Arameans would not help the Ammonites again.

es.L: Y vieron los siervos de Hadad-ezer que habían sido derrotados delante de Israel, e hicieron la paz con David y le sirvieron. Y Aram no quiso ayudar más a los hijos de Amón.
es.B: Cuando los que estaban sometidos a Hadad-ezer vieron que Israel los había derrotado, hicieron la paz con David y quedaron sometidos a él. Después de esto los arameos no quisieron volver a ayudar a los amonitas.
es.R: Los pueblos que habían servido a Hadad-ezer vieron que Israel los había vencido. Así que hicieron la paz con David y desde entonces le sirvieron a él. Después de eso, los arameos no quisieron volver a ayudar a los amonitas.

fr.L: Et les serviteurs d’Hadadézer virent qu’ils avaient été battus devant Israël, et ils firent la paix avec David et le servirent. Et Aram ne voulut plus porter secours aux fils d’Ammon.
fr.B: Quand les vassaux d’Hadadézer virent qu’Israël les avait battus, ils firent la paix avec David et lui furent soumis. Après cela, les Araméens ne voulurent plus venir en aide aux Ammonites.
fr.R: Les peuples qui servaient Hadadézer ont vu qu’Israël les avait battus. Alors ils ont fait la paix avec David et ils l’ont servi à la place. Après cela, les Araméens n’ont plus voulu aider les Ammonites.

sw.L: Watumishi wa Hadadezeri walipoona kwamba wameshindwa mbele ya Israeli, wakafanya amani na Daudi wakamtumikia. Nao Aramu hawakutaka kuwasaidia wana wa Amoni tena.
sw.B: Wale waliokuwa chini ya Hadadezeri walipoona kwamba Israeli wamewashinda, walifanya amani na Daudi, wakawa chini yake. Baada ya hayo Waaramu hawakutaka kuwasaidia Waamoni tena.
sw.R: Watu waliokuwa wakimtumikia Hadadezeri waliona kwamba Israeli wamewashinda. Basi wakafanya amani na Daudi, wakamtumikia yeye badala yake. Baada ya hapo, Waaramu hawakutaka kuwasaidia Waamoni tena.

vi.L: Các đầy tớ của Ha-đa-đê-xe thấy mình đã bị đánh bại trước mặt Y-sơ-ra-ên, thì làm hòa với Đa-vít và phục dịch ông. A-ram không còn muốn giúp con cháu Am-môn nữa.
vi.B: Khi những người thần phục Ha-đa-đê-xe thấy mình đã bị Y-sơ-ra-ên đánh bại, họ làm hòa với Đa-vít và thần phục ông. Từ đó người A-ram không còn muốn giúp người Am-môn nữa.
vi.R: Những người trước kia phục vụ Ha-đa-đê-xe thấy Y-sơ-ra-ên đã đánh bại mình. Vì vậy họ làm hòa với Đa-vít và quay sang phục vụ ông. Sau đó, người A-ram không chịu giúp người Am-môn nữa.

ko.L: 그리고 하닷에셀의 종들이 자기들이 이스라엘 앞에서 졌다는 것을 보고, 다윗과 화친하고 그를 섬겼다. 그리고 아람은 다시는 암몬 자손을 돕기를 원하지 않았다.
ko.B: 하닷에셀에게 매여 있던 이들은 자기들이 이스라엘에게 진 것을 알고, 다윗과 화친하고 그를 섬겼다. 그 뒤로 아람 사람들은 다시는 암몬 사람들을 도우려 하지 않았다.
ko.R: 하닷에셀을 섬기던 사람들은 이스라엘에게 졌다는 것을 알았다. 그래서 그들은 다윗과 평화 조약을 맺고 이제는 다윗을 섬겼다. 그 뒤로 아람 사람들은 다시는 암몬 사람들을 돕지 않으려 했다.

pt.L: E os servos de Hadadezer viram que tinham sido derrotados diante de Israel, e fizeram paz com Davi e o serviram. E Arã não quis mais socorrer os filhos de Amom.
pt.B: Quando os vassalos de Hadadezer viram que Israel os tinha derrotado, fizeram paz com Davi e se tornaram seus súditos. Depois disso os arameus não quiseram mais ajudar os amonitas.
pt.R: Os povos que estavam a serviço de Hadadezer viram que Israel os tinha vencido. Então fizeram paz com Davi e passaram a servi-lo. Depois disso, os arameus não quiseram ajudar os amonitas outra vez.

decisions.choice: the servants of Hadadezer: rulers and peoples bound to serve him
decisions.reason: Here "servants" names those who owed loyalty and tribute to Hadadezer as their overlord; 2 Samuel 10:19 calls them "all the kings, the servants of Hadadezer". After the battle they owed the same service to David.

decisions.choice: differences from 2 Samuel 10:19
decisions.reason: Samuel says "all the kings" made peace "with Israel" and served "them", and that Aram "was afraid" to help Ammon any more. Chronicles has "the servants of Hadadezer", says they made peace "with David" and served "him", and says Aram "was not willing" to help.

decisions.choice: Ammon left to fight alone
decisions.reason: With its allies gone, Ammon now faced David by itself. The story goes on in 20:1, when Joab besieges Rabbah.

decisions.choice: servants (Literal); those who were subject to (Balanced); the people who had served (Readable)
decisions.reason: These "servants" are subject rulers and peoples, not officials or envoys, so Balanced and Readable describe their position instead.

decisions.choice: os servos (L), os vassalos (B), os povos que estavam a serviço (R); com Davi; não quis
decisions.reason: 2 Samuel 10:19 in Portuguese ("servos" at Literal, "vassalos" at Balanced), with Chronicles' changes (m2): no "todos os reis", so Readable says "os povos" (m1); peace "com Davi" and service to him; and Aram "não quis" rather than "teve medo".
